note: Reasoned exemptions from the consumer DX contract (`ui-cli check consumer-dx`). Each entry waives one rule for one component and states why. An entry that stops matching a real defect fails the check as a stale exception, so the list can only shrink by fixing the component.

exceptions.reason: Controlled only by design: `value` and `onValueChange` are required, so the page always owns the selection and an uncontrolled default has no caller yet. Waived until a consumer needs to mount it with an initial segment.
The group renders a plain `div` and its props type declares no `ref`, so a consumer cannot focus or measure it. Fixing it means typing the group as a host element; tracked outside this contract wave.

`SegmentedControlProps` is a closed interface that inherits no host type and destructures no rest, so `id`, `data-*` and `aria-*` are rejected. Same fix as `ref`: extend the host element the group renders.
The field types its props as a closed interface and exposes no `ref`; focusing the input from the page needs a ref it does not offer yet.
`AutocompleteProps` extends no host type and the component spreads no rest, so standard attributes never reach an element.
`SelectFieldProps` extends `FieldStateProps` only, so it carries no `ref` and the trigger cannot be focused from the page.
`SelectFieldProps` extends `FieldStateProps` only and the component spreads no rest, so `id` and `data-*` reach no element.
`MultiSelectFieldProps` extends `FieldStateProps` only, so it carries no `ref` and the trigger cannot be focused from the page.
`MultiSelectFieldProps` extends `FieldStateProps` only and the component spreads no rest, so `id` and `data-*` reach no element.
`DatePickerFieldProps` is `FieldStateProps` intersected with its own members, so it carries no `ref` and the trigger cannot be focused from the page.
`DatePickerFieldProps` inherits no host type, so standard attributes are rejected by the type even where the component spreads a rest.
